# Joseph and Aseneth Chapter 7 — The EMET Bible (Literal)
**Translator:** EMET | **Source:** Greek MS | **Section:** Aseneth Rises on the Eighth Day

---

**7:1** And it came-to-pass on the eighth day, when the dawn was still dark and the cock had not yet crowed, that Aseneth arose from her bed, for she had no more strength to weep.

**7:2** And she said to herself: 'What shall I do? Behold, I have no one to whom I can flee and be saved. All men hate me, and my father Pentephres has betrothed me to the first-born son of Pharaoh, and Joseph hates me, because I worshiped dead idols.'

**7:3** 'I will go to my father's God, the God of Joseph, and I will cry to him, and he will hear me, for he is the Father of all orphans and a Protector of all the afflicted and a Helper of all who are oppressed.'

**7:4** And Aseneth arose and went to the east window and looked toward the east, and behold, the sun was rising and the morning star was shining in the sky.

**7:5** And she said: 'Lord, the God of the ages, who created all things and breathed-in to them the breath of life, who brought the invisible things to light, who made all things and set them in order — to you I cry out, Lord, like a little child who has no father and mother, and whom a stranger has taken captive.'

**7:6** 'For my father and mother deny me, because I destroyed and shattered their gods. And I have no other hope except in you, Lord, and no other refuge except your mercy, Lord God.'

**7:7** And Aseneth arose and took her linen garments from the floor and put on a mourning garment, and tied about her a black garment that was old and torn, and girded herself with sackcloth.

**7:8** And she took off the golden crown from her head and the golden bracelets from her hands and the golden anklets from her feet, and cast all these on the floor.

**7:9** And she scattered ashes upon her head and fell to the floor and beat her breast and wept bitterly.

**7:10** And she prayed to the Lord God of Joseph and said: 'Lord God of the ages, the God who made-alive and called the living, who called from the darkness to the light and from error to truth and from death to life — Lord, you alone are gracious and kind and longsuffering and most merciful and gentle, more than all men and all gods.'

**7:11** 'To you, Lord, I flee for refuge, and to you I offer my petition, and to you I cry out, Lord, and before you I confess my sins and the impiety of my fathers.'

**7:12** 'Have mercy on me, Lord, for I have sinned greatly before you, and I am an impious woman who served dead and dumb idols. Have mercy on me, Lord, the desolate and the afflicted one.'

---
*EMET: hyphenated compounds; chapter:verse format.*
